core.title: Performance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue deterioration subjected to TNT equivalent BLEVE loads
core.abstract: During the service life, bridges are subjected to long-term fatigue loads induced by heavy-duty vehicles, while simultaneously facing the threat of accidental explosions resulting from warfare, improper transportation of hazardous materials, or traffic accidents. It is widely known that fatigue causes material damage and degradation of structural performance. Unfortunately, the accumulated fatigue damage has not been considered for estimating the dynamic behaviour of the bridge deck. This study proposes a numerical method to evaluate the blast resistance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue damage subjected to boiling liquid expanding vapour explosion (BLEVE) loads by the TNT equivalent method. First, the finite element models of T-beam bridge decks are established to analyse the influence of fatigue on their blast performance. The results indicate that fatigue significantly weakens the blast resistance of the T-beam bridge decks (with the mid-span displacement increasing by up to 2 times). This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the differences in the energy dissipation mechanisms. Second, parametric analysis indicates that TNT equivalence is the most sensitive parameter, with an amplification effect of up to 1.8 times. Finally, based on machine learning techniques optimised via 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, a predictive model for the maximum displacement of fatigue-damaged T-beam bridge decks under blast loading is established. This study provides a reliable and efficient approach for the damage assessment of long-term service bridges under blast loading.
core.summary: 该研究关注长期服役桥梁累积疲劳损伤后遭遇偶然爆炸的抗爆表现。作者以TNT当量法表征沸腾液体膨胀蒸气爆炸荷载，建立T梁桥面板有限元模型，并开展参数分析与机器学习位移预测。摘要报告疲劳削弱抗爆能力，将响应差异主要归因于耗能机制，并指出TNT当量是最敏感参数。解读：研究将服役劣化与突发荷载联合考虑，对既有桥梁风险评估具有参考价值；但摘要不足以核验模型验证及预测精度。[摘要]

core.title: Beyond SELEX: AI-driven aptamers from sequence to structure to function.
core.abstract: Conventional aptamer discovery by systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is often constrained by limited library capacity, PCR bias, and multi-round screening. The recent convergence of artificial intelligence with aptamer development is driving a paradigm shift from empirical screening toward rational, data-driven design. This Review presents a timely and comprehensive overview of AI integration across the entire aptamer development pipeline, with a particular emphasis on advances reported in 2024-2026. We begin by discussing bioinformatics databases and computational tools for high-throughput SELEX data analysis. We then review state-of-the-art strategies for secondary and tertiary structure prediction, including recent breakthroughs such as AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFoldNA, and diffusion-based approaches. We also cover machine learning methods for aptamer-target interaction prediction, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations. A major focus is placed on very recent AI-driven generative design, including diffusion models (AptaDiff), language model-based frameworks (InstructNA, GRAPE-LM), and reinforcement learning approaches (AiDTA) for de novo aptamer generation and optimization. Emerging applications of AI-designed aptamers in precision diagnostics, targeted therapy, and biosensing are also surveyed. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future directions toward closed-loop, interpretable AI frameworks for translational aptamer development. By synthesizing the latest computational and experimental advances, this Review aims to serve as a timely resource for researchers seeking to leverage AI for next-generation aptamer discovery.

core.title: Physics-Guided Machine Learning for Joint Fault Diagnosis in Inverter-Fed Induction Motor Drives
core.abstract: In intelligent electric vehicle (EV) traction drives, pulse-width modulation and field-oriented control (FOC) introduce broadband harmonics and non-stationary start-up transients. These dynamics obscure incipient inter-turn stator faults (ITSF), particularly when inverter switch failures and measurement interference co-occur. To meet the low-latency requirements of on-board vehicle control units (VCUs), this paper proposes a data-centric, physics-guided diagnosis pipeline. Relying exclusively on current measurements, the framework jointly detects and localises ITSF (1–3% severity), open-circuit IGBT faults, and additive white Gaussian noise (5–20 dB SNR). A compact 27-dimensional feature vector is constructed by fusing db4 discrete wavelet transform sub-band energies, residualised negative-sequence phasors, αβ hodograph descriptors, and harmonic energy ratios. This targeted extraction empowers an ensemble of bagged decision trees to perform lightweight classification suitable for embedded edge hardware. In a simulation-based evaluation across four scenarios (transient and steady state, with and without AWGN), the pipeline achieves cross-validated accuracies of 91.63–98.97% and hold-out test accuracies of 93.13–98.75%. Unlike traditional threshold detectors that conflate inverter or sensing artefacts with ITSF, this approach achieves subsystem-level localisation across motor, inverter, and sensing hardware, providing the reliable condition monitoring required for cyber–physical EV digital twins.

core.title: Vibration fatigue analysis in mechanical structures using AI: Trends, challenges, and future opportunities
core.abstract: During their service life, mechanical equipment used in fields such as offshore engineering is subjected to complex vibration loads induced by wind and waves, leading to the accumulation of fatigue damage and posing a serious threat to equipment safety. Therefore, conducting vibration fatigue damage analysis is of practical importance for ensuring equipment safety. In recent years, with the advancement of AI, new solutions have emerged for damage analysis, creating an urgent need to systematically review existing methodology. This paper reviews recent research progress across four dimensions. Firstly, it discusses the mechanical structures subject to vibration damage analysis. Subsequently, it summarises research on damage assessment, damage detection, service life prediction and reliability analysis from the perspectives of both traditional methods and machine learning approaches. Finally, it analyses the transition from traditional methods towards AI-driven approaches, along with the challenges faced, and identifies potential directions for future research. This review aims to provide researchers in the field of vibration fatigue analysis with a systematic methodological reference, highlighting the potential of AI to drive the evolution of traditional methods towards intelligent analysis. It seeks to support the development of vibration fatigue damage analysis methods in fields such as marine engineering.

core.title: Scientific Machine Learning-Based Climate-Adaptive Co-Design of Electric Bus Charging Infrastructure and Control
core.abstract: Electric bus operators must limit charging-infrastructure investment while supplying enough layover energy to preserve battery reserves during service. Climate changes both energy demand and charging acceptance, linking forecasts to control and infrastructure selection. We propose a scientific machine learning (SciML) framework for climate-adaptive co-design that predicts bus energy from an equipment-based physical prior and multimodal residual learning. Day-level calibration converts forecasts into upper energies that determine inventory targets and charging-window commitments; linear-programming screening is followed by closed-loop qualification of site sets. Public weather and reconstructed Montréal and Singapore duties drive continuous-year simulation with one vehicle configuration. With 28 target fitting days plus 40 calibration days, Singapore-to-Montréal transfer lowers 2025 forecast error by 5.4% against full fine-tuning and 18.7% against gradient boosting. Removing the physical prior and route-network inputs raises error 2.3 to 3.0 times. In 2025, reverse transfer lowers error by 58.0% against the calibrated physical prior and remains 11.3% above gradient boosting. Prediction accuracy and reserve outcomes rank the frozen predictors differently. On Singapore's eight-site design under fixed control in 2025, gradient boosting has the lowest forecast error but 135.03 lost days per operating seed, compared with 9.80 for transfer and 0.43 for the calibrated physical prior. Lost days count failures beyond a forecast-free full-site Reference plus uncommitted dates. Predictor-specific control pairing lowers transfer's lost days from 9.80 to 0.30. In Montréal, qualification restores the terminal needed on the coldest development day. The qualified eight-site predictive design lowers annual charging-subsystem cost by 28.2% against the full-site Reference.

core.title: From preventive to predictive maintenance : application and comparison of machine learning models
core.abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει την εξέλιξη της συντήρησης του βιομηχανικού εξοπλισμού από τις παραδοσιακές στρατηγικές προς την προγνωστική συντήρηση. Αρχικά παρουσιάζονται η διορθωτική, η προληπτική, η βάσει κατάστασης και η προγνωστική συντήρηση καθώς και ο ρόλος των λειτουργικών δεδομένων, των αισθητήρων και της παρακολούθησης κατάστασης.Στη συνέχεια εξετάζεται η χρήση της Μηχανικής Μάθησης για την αναγνώριση βλαβών και παρουσιάζονται η Λογιστική Παλινδρόμηση, το Δέντρο Απόφασης, το Τυχαίο Δάσος και το Πολυεπίπεδο Perceptron. Στο εφαρμοσμένο μέρος χρησιμοποιείται το συνθετικό σύνολο δεδομένων AI4I 2020. Η αρχική εξέταση έδειξε ότι το dataset έχει καθαρή και οργανωμένη δομή αλλά παρουσιάζει έντονη ανισορροπία, καθώς μόνο το 3.39% των παρατηρήσεων αντιστοιχεί σε βλάβη. Μετά την κατάλληλη προεπεξεργασία, τα τέσσερα μοντέλαεκπαιδεύτηκαν και αξιολογήθηκαν στο ίδιο σύνολο δοκιμής. Τα αποτελέσματα έδειξαν διαφορετική συμπεριφορά μεταξύ των μοντέλων. Το Τυχαίο Δάσος παρουσίασε την υψηλότερη precision, τον μεγαλύτερο δείκτη F1 και το υψηλότερο PR-AUC. Αντίθετα, το Πολυεπίπεδο Perceptron παρουσίασε την υψηλότερη ανάκληση και το υψηλότερο ROC-AUC, εντοπίζοντας 61 από τις 68 πραγματικές βλάβες. Συνολικά, η εργασία δείχνει ότι η επιλογή ενός μοντέλου προγνωστικής συντήρησης πρέπει να λαμβάνει υπόψη τόσο την ικανότητα ανίχνευσης βλαβών όσο και τον αριθμό των ψευδών συναγερμών.

papers.title: Performance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue deterioration subjected to TNT equivalent BLEVE loads
papers.abstract: During the service life, bridges are subjected to long-term fatigue loads induced by heavy-duty vehicles, while simultaneously facing the threat of accidental explosions resulting from warfare, improper transportation of hazardous materials, or traffic accidents. Unfortunately, the accumulated fatigue damage has not been considered for estimating the dynamic behaviour of the bridge deck. This study proposes a numerical method to evaluate the blast resistance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue damage subjected to boiling liquid expanding vapour explosion (BLEVE) loads by the TNT equivalent method. First, the finite element models of T-beam bridge decks are established to analyse the influence of fatigue on their blast performance. The results indicate that fatigue significantly weakens the blast resistance of the T-beam bridge decks (with the mid-span displacement increasing by up to 2 times). This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the differences in the energy dissipation mechanisms. Second, parametric analysis indicates that TNT equivalence is the most sensitive parameter, with an amplification effect of up to 1.8 times. Finally, based on machine learning techniques optimised via 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, a predictive model for the maximum displacement of fatigue-damaged T-beam bridge decks under blast loading is established. This study provides a reliable and efficient approach for the damage assessment of long-term service bridges under blast loading.

First, the finite element models of T-beam bridge decks are established to analyse the influence of fatigue on their blast performance. The results indicate that fatigue significantly weakens the blast resistance of the T-beam bridge decks (with the mid-span displacement increasing by up to 2 times). This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the differences in the energy dissipation mechanisms. Second, parametric analysis indicates that TNT equivalence is the most sensitive parameter, with an amplification effect of up to 1.8 times. Finally, based on machine learning techniques optimised via 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, a predictive model for the maximum displacement of fatigue-damaged T-beam bridge decks under blast loading is established. This study provides a reliable and efficient approach for the damage assessment of long-term service bridges under blast loading.

papers.title: Beyond SELEX: AI-driven aptamers from sequence to structure to function.
papers.abstract: Conventional aptamer discovery by systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is often constrained by limited library capacity, PCR bias, and multi-round screening. The recent convergence of artificial intelligence with aptamer development is driving a paradigm shift from empirical screening toward rational, data-driven design. This Review presents a timely and comprehensive overview of AI integration across the entire aptamer development pipeline, with a particular emphasis on advances reported in 2024-2026. We begin by discussing bioinformatics databases and computational tools for high-throughput SELEX data analysis. We then review state-of-the-art strategies for secondary and tertiary structure prediction, including recent breakthroughs such as AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFoldNA, and diffusion-based approaches. We also cover machine learning methods for aptamer-target interaction prediction, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations. A major focus is placed on very recent AI-driven generative design, including diffusion models (AptaDiff), language model-based frameworks (InstructNA, GRAPE-LM), and reinforcement learning approaches (AiDTA) for de novo aptamer generation and optimization. Emerging applications of AI-designed aptamers in precision diagnostics, targeted therapy, and biosensing are also surveyed. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future directions toward closed-loop, interpretable AI frameworks for translational aptamer development. By synthesizing the latest computational and experimental advances, this Review aims to serve as a timely resource for researchers seeking to leverage AI for next-generation aptamer discovery.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Machine Learning for Joint Fault Diagnosis in Inverter-Fed Induction Motor Drives
papers.abstract: In intelligent electric vehicle (EV) traction drives, pulse-width modulation and field-oriented control (FOC) introduce broadband harmonics and non-stationary start-up transients. These dynamics obscure incipient inter-turn stator faults (ITSF), particularly when inverter switch failures and measurement interference co-occur. To meet the low-latency requirements of on-board vehicle control units (VCUs), this paper proposes a data-centric, physics-guided diagnosis pipeline. Relying exclusively on current measurements, the framework jointly detects and localises ITSF (1–3% severity), open-circuit IGBT faults, and additive white Gaussian noise (5–20 dB SNR). A compact 27-dimensional feature vector is constructed by fusing db4 discrete wavelet transform sub-band energies, residualised negative-sequence phasors, αβ hodograph descriptors, and harmonic energy ratios. This targeted extraction empowers an ensemble of bagged decision trees to perform lightweight classification suitable for embedded edge hardware. In a simulation-based evaluation across four scenarios (transient and steady state, with and without AWGN), the pipeline achieves cross-validated accuracies of 91.63–98.97% and hold-out test accuracies of 93.13–98.75%. Unlike traditional threshold detectors that conflate inverter or sensing artefacts with ITSF, this approach achieves subsystem-level localisation across motor, inverter, and sensing hardware, providing the reliable condition monitoring required for cyber–physical EV digital twins.

papers.title: Vibration fatigue analysis in mechanical structures using AI: Trends, challenges, and future opportunities
papers.abstract: During their service life, mechanical equipment used in fields such as offshore engineering is subjected to complex vibration loads induced by wind and waves, leading to the accumulation of fatigue damage and posing a serious threat to equipment safety. Therefore, conducting vibration fatigue damage analysis is of practical importance for ensuring equipment safety. In recent years, with the advancement of AI, new solutions have emerged for damage analysis, creating an urgent need to systematically review existing methodology. This paper reviews recent research progress across four dimensions. Firstly, it discusses the mechanical structures subject to vibration damage analysis. Subsequently, it summarises research on damage assessment, damage detection, service life prediction and reliability analysis from the perspectives of both traditional methods and machine learning approaches. Finally, it analyses the transition from traditional methods towards AI-driven approaches, along with the challenges faced, and identifies potential directions for future research. This review aims to provide researchers in the field of vibration fatigue analysis with a systematic methodological reference, highlighting the potential of AI to drive the evolution of traditional methods towards intelligent analysis. It seeks to support the development of vibration fatigue damage analysis methods in fields such as marine engineering.

papers.title: Scientific Machine Learning-Based Climate-Adaptive Co-Design of Electric Bus Charging Infrastructure and Control
papers.abstract: Electric bus operators must limit charging-infrastructure investment while supplying enough layover energy to preserve battery reserves during service. Climate changes both energy demand and charging acceptance, linking forecasts to control and infrastructure selection. We propose a scientific machine learning (SciML) framework for climate-adaptive co-design that predicts bus energy from an equipment-based physical prior and multimodal residual learning. Day-level calibration converts forecasts into upper energies that determine inventory targets and charging-window commitments; linear-programming screening is followed by closed-loop qualification of site sets. Public weather and reconstructed Montréal and Singapore duties drive continuous-year simulation with one vehicle configuration. With 28 target fitting days plus 40 calibration days, Singapore-to-Montréal transfer lowers 2025 forecast error by 5.4% against full fine-tuning and 18.7% against gradient boosting. Removing the physical prior and route-network inputs raises error 2.3 to 3.0 times. In 2025, reverse transfer lowers error by 58.0% against the calibrated physical prior and remains 11.3% above gradient boosting. Prediction accuracy and reserve outcomes rank the frozen predictors differently. On Singapore's eight-site design under fixed control in 2025, gradient boosting has the lowest forecast error but 135.03 lost days per operating seed, compared with 9.80 for transfer and 0.43 for the calibrated physical prior. Lost days count failures beyond a forecast-free full-site Reference plus uncommitted dates. Predictor-specific control pairing lowers transfer's lost days from 9.80 to 0.30. In Montréal, qualification restores the terminal needed on the coldest development day. The qualified eight-site predictive design lowers annual charging-subsystem cost by 28.2% against the full-site Reference.

papers.title: From preventive to predictive maintenance : application and comparison of machine learning models
papers.abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει την εξέλιξη της συντήρησης του βιομηχανικού εξοπλισμού από τις παραδοσιακές στρατηγικές προς την προγνωστική συντήρηση. Αρχικά παρουσιάζονται η διορθωτική, η προληπτική, η βάσει κατάστασης και η προγνωστική συντήρηση καθώς και ο ρόλος των λειτουργικών δεδομένων, των αισθητήρων και της παρακολούθησης κατάστασης.Στη συνέχεια εξετάζεται η χρήση της Μηχανικής Μάθησης για την αναγνώριση βλαβών και παρουσιάζονται η Λογιστική Παλινδρόμηση, το Δέντρο Απόφασης, το Τυχαίο Δάσος και το Πολυεπίπεδο Perceptron. Στο εφαρμοσμένο μέρος χρησιμοποιείται το συνθετικό σύνολο δεδομένων AI4I 2020. Η αρχική εξέταση έδειξε ότι το dataset έχει καθαρή και οργανωμένη δομή αλλά παρουσιάζει έντονη ανισορροπία, καθώς μόνο το 3.39% των παρατηρήσεων αντιστοιχεί σε βλάβη. Μετά την κατάλληλη προεπεξεργασία, τα τέσσερα μοντέλαεκπαιδεύτηκαν και αξιολογήθηκαν στο ίδιο σύνολο δοκιμής. Τα αποτελέσματα έδειξαν διαφορετική συμπεριφορά μεταξύ των μοντέλων. Το Τυχαίο Δάσος παρουσίασε την υψηλότερη precision, τον μεγαλύτερο δείκτη F1 και το υψηλότερο PR-AUC. Αντίθετα, το Πολυεπίπεδο Perceptron παρουσίασε την υψηλότερη ανάκληση και το υψηλότερο ROC-AUC, εντοπίζοντας 61 από τις 68 πραγματικές βλάβες. Συνολικά, η εργασία δείχνει ότι η επιλογή ενός μοντέλου προγνωστικής συντήρησης πρέπει να λαμβάνει υπόψη τόσο την ικανότητα ανίχνευσης βλαβών όσο και τον αριθμό των ψευδών συναγερμών.
